name: Fibonacci retracement
seoTitle: Fibonacci retracement Calculator — Formula, Units & Example
seoDesc: Fibonacci retracement: answer 33 values and the page computes the result when you press Calculate — formula and worked example included.
summary: The Fibonacci retracement calculator is a free, no-sign-up finance tool. Fill in the 4 fields it asks for and it works out high price straight away, with the formula shown underneath. That makes it useful for a budget, a loan conversation, a payslip check or a what-if before you talk to a lender. Nothing repaints underneath you: edit a field, press Calculate, and the new answer appears. That is how you find out which input the result is sensitive to.

sections.title: How does the Fibonacci retracement calculator work?
sections.html:
The Fibonacci retracement calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports high price in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the trend direction and the type of Fibonacci levels); then you type in the figures it asks for.

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Fibonacci retracement calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

High price=low price + price difference
0%=high price
23.6%=high price − 59 ÷ 250 × price difference
High price=(191 ÷ 500) × price difference + 38.2%
50%=high price − 1 ÷ 2 × price difference
Price difference=(500 ÷ 309) × high price − 500 ÷ 309 × 61.8%

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Suppose Trend direction set to Uptrend, Type of Fibonacci levels set to Retracement levels, Low price = 10 and Price difference = 10. Working through the relationship above gives High price = 20, 0% = 20, 23.6% = 18 and 38.2% = 16.

Read it as a template. Every number above can be replaced with one of yours; only the relationship between them is fixed.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: High price = 20, 0% = 20, 23.6% = 18 and 38.2% = 16 should be roughly the size you expected from Trend direction set to Uptrend and Type of Fibonacci levels set to Retracement levels.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Fibonacci retracement calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Building a monthly budget and testing how one number shifts the rest
  • Sizing up a purchase before you commit to it
  • Preparing questions for a lender, an accountant or an adviser

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.

faq.q: What does the Fibonacci retracement calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns high price. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Fibonacci retracement calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for a few values, which is 4 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter low price in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Low price opens in US Dollar and the chip beside it offers 113 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (2 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports High price = 20. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Fibonacci retracement calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
